Combustion

/kum-BUS-chun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Combustion means the process of burning.

Combustion means the process of burning. A car engine converts the combustion of fuel into the motion of pistons thousands of times a minute.

Worked Example

For the science fair, Amara lowered a glass jar over a burning candle and started her stopwatch. The flame shrank, guttered, and died in eleven seconds. Her poster explained the result: combustion needs oxygen, and the sealed jar held only so much. When the oxygen ran out, the burning simply stopped.

The candle demonstration is entirely about burning as a chemical process that requires oxygen — which is what combustion names.

How Combustion Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

burning

burning: the process of being consumed by fire

ignition

ignition: the act of catching fire

Antonyms

extinguishing

extinguishing: the putting out of a fire

quenching

quenching: the act of smothering flames

How Strong Is It? — smoldering → combustion → detonation

smoldering vs. combustion

smoldering vs. combustion: Smoldering is slow, flameless burning — the quiet low end of combustion.

detonation vs. combustion

detonation vs. combustion: A detonation is combustion at its most violent — burning so fast it becomes an explosion.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of combustion.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — com-

Prefix — com-: together; thoroughly (Latin)

Root — bust-

Root — bust-: to burn (Latin urere/comburere, 'to burn up')

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: process of

Put it together

Put it together: Combustion comes from Latin comburere, 'to burn up' — com- ('thoroughly') plus a form of urere, 'to burn.' Outside its own small family (combust, combustible), this burn-root left no common English words, and despite appearances it is completely unrelated to the slang word 'bust.'

Use the root in a new word: combustible

Use the root in a new word: combustible: Anything combustible — able to catch fire — carries the same Latin burn-root as combustion itself.

Word Building

Word Choice

scientific, technical

Combustion names the chemical process of burning at any scale — a match tip, an engine cylinder, a rocket nozzle. Keep it apart from conflagration (another word in this unit), which is not a process but an event: a huge, uncontrolled, destructive fire.
